title: Codex runtime adapter
description: Objective: add a capability-probed Codex provider with pinned runtime closure, structured/raw events, cancellation, and reconciliation parity. Deliverable: focused runner Codex modules plus golden streams. NOT in scope: Gemini or provider marketplace. Hard dependency: proven Claude adapter contract and Foundation effect supervisor. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/providers/codex/** and packages/testkit/src/providers/codex/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: Probe and runtime closure are immutable and every unproven capability is typed UNSUPPORTED.
Effect identity, raw events, cwd/process observation, cancellation, and crash reconciliation match the provider contract.
No provider output grants authority or satisfies verification.
taskRails: Portability consumes frozen daemon/core contracts; adapters cannot fork lifecycle or authority semantics.
Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP only; no custom MCP-over-WebSocket dialect.
Unsupported OS/provider/import facts remain typed UNSUPPORTED or UNKNOWN, never guessed.
IDE adapters are thin optional shells for the standalone control room. Keep files below 400 lines and use explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Explore and pin. Read every module under packages/runner/src/providers/claude/ — claude-observation, claude-capabilities, claude-probe, claude-stream-anomalies, claude-stream, claude-render, claude-cancel-reconcile — and mem:task-task-5ff2b39df70c4451ae07a44c92935b42-handoff, which records the decisions that must not be re-litigated. Read packages/testkit/src/providers/claude/claude-golden-streams.ts for the cross-package corpus protocol. Read packages/runner/src/supervisor/ (effect-kernel, effect-shape, effect-activation, effect-lifecycle, drain-reconciliation, restart-reconstruction) to confirm the seam this adapter must NOT cross: cancellation is an INPUT and process death is a caller-supplied observation. Verify every symbol you intend to name actually exists — the governor's promotion note is explicit that the parent shell's description never described code. Confirm the shape of ClaudeProcessExit (EXITED{code} | SIGNALLED{signal} | UNOBSERVED) and CLAUDE_RECONCILED_OUTCOMES, which the parity step will compare against. Produce no files.
implementationPlan.note: No files produced. Read the seven Claude production modules and golden corpus protocol, plus supervisor effect-kernel/effect-shape/effect-activation/effect-lifecycle/drain-reconciliation/restart-reconstruction. Verified exact production seams: probeClaudeRuntime, recordClaudeStream, renderClaudeContext, reconcileClaudeRun; ClaudeProcessExit is EXITED{code}|SIGNALLED{signal}|UNOBSERVED; CLAUDE_RECONCILED_OUTCOMES has six frozen values. Confirmed supervisor remains pure and imports the Claude exit/outcome strings structurally; Codex parity must preserve those strings and must not import/cross the supervisor. Confirmed Claude adapter has zero child_process/spawn/.kill/clock/random hits and bridges are exact LF one-liners. Golden corpus is marker-delimited JSON, raw-byte sha256, DEVELOPMENT_ONLY/NOT_CONFIRMATORY, CRLF retained in base64, no testkit bridge. Owned Codex directories were absent/clean at HEAD 82f4a354. Baselines: runner 30 files/980 tests; testkit 18 files/234 tests. Design §11.5 confirms Codex JSONL is only an adapter fact and capability claims require observation. For the plan-required provider difference, Codex will add a narrowly observed CWD_OBSERVATION record/status (requestedCwd must equal observedCwd); all unproven fields remain required-null and UNSUPPORTED.

implementationPlan.description: codex-observation.ts — ProviderRuntimeObservation plus the shared failure shape, mirroring claude-observation.ts. Declare CODEX_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_VERSION = "moe-codex-runtime-observation/1", the closure/pinning/truth vocabularies, bounded constants, and CodexFailure<Code> / codexFailure as the ONE rejection shape for this whole adapter. DO NOT import claudeFailure: adapters are per-provider and independently replaceable, and importing one provider's module into another couples two things that must be able to diverge. Mirror it structurally instead; step 9 proves the two stay congruent. Carry forward two decisions from the Claude handoff, both load-bearing: the runtime closure is SORTED BY PATH BEFORE HASHING, because discovery order is not a fact about the runtime and letting it into the observation digest would make the wrapper's pre-activate comparison report drift that never happened — and duplicate paths are REFUSED, never deduped. And truthClass is INDEPENDENT of pinningMethod: an honestly observed runtime that cannot be pinned is still honestly observed, so keep the launch question a separate predicate. Guard a lying probe port: a non-array closure or non-record entry returns a typed failure rather than crashing on .length. Keep under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note: TDD scope sequencing: created the owned observation test one step early so production did not precede RED. RED was an assertion failure (`existsSync=false`) before the module existed; GREEN after minimal module; then implemented the full 200-line observation surface and 6 focused tests. It mirrors Claude structurally without imports, sorts closure paths before digesting, refuses duplicates, guards non-array/non-record probe claims, keeps truth independent of pinning, deep-freezes output, exports a digest-input record excluding the digest itself, and has one frozen CodexFailure shape. Focused suite 1 file/6 tests and runner typecheck both exit 0. No supervisor or Claude path touched.

implementationPlan.description: codex-capabilities.ts — the closed capability vocabulary and proof rules. This is DoD 1: every unproven capability is typed UNSUPPORTED, never guessed, which is also task rail 3. Mirror claude-capabilities.ts: a frozen capability list, statuses SUPPORTED | UNSUPPORTED with no third arm, proof methods, and an UNPROVEN_PROBE_REPORT constant that is the safe default. THE CENTRAL RULE, carried from Claude: PROOF IS OBSERVATION, NOT CLAIM. The probe port returns observation records, and a record that contradicts its own claim proves the OPPOSITE — childrenAfter > 0 makes PROCESS_TREE_TERMINATION UNSUPPORTED regardless of what the CLI advertises. Help text is carried for diagnostics and proves nothing. Pin RESUME to UNSUPPORTED in v1 as Claude does. Probe-report fields are REQUIRED AND NULLABLE, never optional: with exactOptionalPropertyTypes an omitted field reads as a deliberate absence, so a port that forgot to observe something would be indistinguishable from one that proved it absent. Tests assert the specific capability code AND the status, never merely that something was unsupported. Keep under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note: TDD RED asserted the missing capability module (`existsSync=false`), then GREEN and expanded to 6 behavioral tests. The 216-line module publishes a frozen 12-capability Codex vocabulary, exact SUPPORTED|UNSUPPORTED statuses, closed proof methods, required-nullable CodexProbeReport, and fully explicit UNPROVEN_PROBE_REPORT. CWD_OBSERVATION is the one provider-specific addition demanded by the objective; only requestedCwd===observedCwd proves it. Help/resume claims prove nothing; RESUME is pinned UNSUPPORTED. Contradicting cwd and childrenAfter>0 records explicitly produce their named capability with UNSUPPORTED/NONE. Focused Codex suites 2 files/12 tests and runner typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: codex-probe.ts — probeCodexRuntime, binding the capability profile to the runtime observation, mirroring claude-probe.ts (the smallest module at 120 lines, so this should stay compact). The profile and the observation must be bound to each other so a capability claim cannot be read against a different runtime than the one observed. The result is immutable — DoD 1 requires probe and runtime closure be immutable, so freeze deeply and assert it. A probe that cannot observe returns UNPROVEN_PROBE_REPORT rather than a partially filled one.
implementationPlan.note: TDD RED asserted the missing codex-probe.ts module, then GREEN and expanded to 6 probe tests. The compact 114-line probe binds profile.capabilitySchemaDigest into the runtime observation, deeply freezes profile/closure/result, maps thrown, partial, and hostile nested probe reports to the complete UNPROVEN report, and preserves a lying non-array closure as the stable CODEX_OBSERVATION_CLOSURE_INVALID refusal rather than a crash. Missing capability lookup returns UNSUPPORTED. Focused Codex suites: 3 files/18 tests; runner typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: codex-stream.ts — structured/raw dual record with bounded retention, mirroring claude-stream.ts and claude-stream-anomalies.ts. Split framing and the anomaly vocabulary into a sibling module if the file approaches 250 lines. FOUR DECISIONS FROM CLAUDE THAT MUST NOT BE SIMPLIFIED, each of which was a real bug: GAP is computed over the SET of sequences, not delivery order, or out-of-order delivery (1,3,2) falsely raises GAP; a malformed record COUNTS as occupying a slot, or (1, unreadable, 3) invents a gap; COUNTER_REGRESSION suppresses gap analysis entirely, because contiguity is undefined across a restart; and the first record establishes the origin and is never gap-checked, so RESUME_DISCONTINUITY keys on an explicit resumedFrom and never on 'first seq != 1'. Retention is bounded but digest coverage is not: past the size cap the record flips to an artifact reference while sha256 and byteLength still span every byte, and per-event line bytes are suppressed too — omitting that reintroduces the unbounded buffer through the back door. Bound the event COUNT as well as the byte size; Claude needed a separate event-limit refusal because the events array was unbounded even when raw retention was capped. Keep UNKNOWN_SCHEMA distinct from any pre-activation refusal code.
implementationPlan.note: TDD RED asserted the missing stream module, then GREEN and expanded to 11 stream tests. Split framing/anomalies (156 lines) from retention/recording (170 lines). Tests pin: out-of-order set analysis without false GAP; real GAP; malformed occupying a slot; counter regression suppressing gap; explicit resumedFrom only; UNKNOWN_SCHEMA separate from PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED; exact raw digest across CRLF; frozen effect-bound events; >16MiB artifact-ref with 64KiB tail and suppressed lineBase64; event-count refusal; stable invalid bytes/effect/allowlist codes. Focused stream suite 1 file/11 tests and runner typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: testkit codex golden streams. Create packages/testkit/src/providers/codex/codex-golden-streams.ts using the EXACT cross-package protocol claude-golden-streams.ts established, because runner tests CANNOT import testkit TypeScript (rootDir "src" plus composite puts the file outside the project). The corpus is ONE JSON document inside a template literal between two marker comments, both exported as string constants; runner tests readFileSync the module, lastIndexOf both markers, slice and JSON.parse. CRITICAL AND COUNTERINTUITIVE: each case's sha256 is over the RAW DECODED BYTES, not canonical JSON. That is deliberate — it means the reader needs only a sha256 implementation, so runner's canonicalJson and testkit's canonicalize never have to agree byte-for-byte, and a cross-package gate that depended on two independent canonicalizers agreeing would be a latent trap. Keep corpus-level stability in-package by pinning a corpus digest constant. Mark the corpus DEVELOPMENT_ONLY. Do NOT add a .js bridge for this file and do NOT touch packages/testkit/src/index.ts — claude-golden-streams.ts has neither, because the corpus is not on the testkit entrypoint and nothing loads it from the Node runtime path. Include at least one CRLF case; Claude's round-trips byte-exact and proved the framing.
implementationPlan.note: TDD RED asserted the missing corpus module, then GREEN and expanded coverage. Added the exact marker-delimited, single-JSON cross-package corpus protocol with 9 DEVELOPMENT_ONLY/NOT_CONFIRMATORY cases. Each sha256 is recomputed over decoded raw bytes; corpus identity pinned to 2b006bc964f353f77e5e1f1d433657bbe29b8ea2827b9fef91e3b28350ab5fc2. Complete carries exactly 3 literal CRLF pairs. Runner reads source via lastIndexOf markers, independently re-verifies byte length/hash, asserts GOLDEN.size=9, and pins all typed outcomes. Testkit corpus gets no bridge and testkit index stayed clean. Focused two suites/17 tests plus testkit and runner typechecks exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: codex-render.ts — the deterministic provider-input render, and the module the human's roadmap amendment of 2026-08-07 speaks to directly: the Codex adapter must consume the SAME provider-neutral validated skill snapshot and canonical AGENTS.md contract as Claude, record exact rendered bytes and digest, respect scoped instruction precedence, and never let skill or prompt text grant command or effect authority. Mirror SkillRendererInput structurally with the version literal "moe-skill-renderer-input/1" pinned rather than taking a @moe/skills dependency — that would touch packages/runner/package.json, outside owned paths, and drift is caught by the version-literal refusal. TWO TRAPS: use renderedBase64, NEVER a Uint8Array, because Object.freeze throws on a non-empty typed array AND runner's deepFreeze treats one as a plain record, so a bytes field inside a frozen record crashes at construction. And the render output must have NO command, effect, or lease field to set — assert the EXACT sorted key list so a future field that could carry authority breaks the test rather than slipping in. That assertion is DoD 3. Bound the mirrored skill count and file count, and check the mandatory size BEFORE framing since framing only grows the payload. Wrap any tokenizer port in try/catch and return a typed refusal; a caller exception escaping a function whose contract is typed refusal is a defect. Split before 400 lines — claude-render.ts is 372.
implementationPlan.note: TDD RED asserted the missing renderer, then GREEN and expanded to 9 tests. Split validated skill decoding (117 lines) from deterministic envelope/budget logic (214 lines). Renderer consumes canonical AGENTS.md bytes, task context, and the same pinned provider-neutral skill snapshot version; sorts skills/files by identity; records exact base64 bytes/digest; freezes all returned records; and exposes only the exact 9-key top-level plus exact 7-key layer shape, with authority NONE/advisoryOnly true and no command/effect/lease affordance. Tests pin version/authority/task/digest/count/size/tokenizer reason codes, pre-frame mandatory bound, advisory-only omission, aggregate skill/file limits, deterministic ordering, and throwing tokenizer fail-closed behavior. Focused 1 file/9 tests and runner typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: codex-cancel-reconcile.ts — typed reconciliation outcomes, mirroring claude-cancel-reconcile.ts (131 lines, the shape to match). Declare CODEX_RECONCILIATION_VERSION, the frozen reconciled-outcome vocabulary, the process-exit union (EXITED with code | SIGNALLED with signal | UNOBSERVED) and reconcileCodexRun. THE SUPERVISOR FENCE IS ABSOLUTE HERE: zero child_process, zero spawn, zero .kill, zero Date.now, zero Math.random anywhere in this adapter. Cancellation is an INPUT and process death is a caller-supplied observation — UNOBSERVED is a first-class arm and must never be collapsed into a guess. Launch locks, job-object death proof, ARMED/SUSPECT and relaunch belong to packages/runner/src/supervisor/, which this adapter feeds and must not reimplement (task rail 1: adapters cannot fork lifecycle or authority semantics). Every reconciliation test asserts the specific outcome code, not merely that reconciliation returned something.
implementationPlan.note: TDD RED asserted the missing reconciliation module, then GREEN and expanded to 16 tests. The 97-line pure reconciler mirrors the six Claude outcome strings and the exact EXITED|SIGNALLED|UNOBSERVED union, treating cancellation and process death strictly as caller-supplied facts. Tests pin every table arm by exact outcome code, distinguish UNOBSERVED from clean exit, ensure gaps/unknown schema/resume stay HONEST_UNKNOWN, reach the full non-empty outcome vocabulary, and verify deep freeze/digest binding. Full Codex tree fence grep reports ZERO child_process/spawn/.kill/clock/random hits. Focused 1 file/16 tests and runner typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: PARITY TEST — the step that gives 'reconciliation parity' from the objective real teeth, and the reason mirroring is safe rather than merely duplicative. Both adapters live in @moe/runner, so a single test file CAN import both and compare them directly. Assert, against the PRODUCTION surfaces of both providers and never against a local re-declaration: the reconciled-outcome vocabularies are SET-EQUAL; the process-exit unions admit the same three arms including UNOBSERVED; the capability STATUS vocabulary is set-equal (SUPPORTED | UNSUPPORTED, no third arm on either side); the observation truth classes are set-equal; and the failure record shape is structurally congruent. Assert the compared sets are NON-EMPTY first — a parity test over two empty arrays passes while proving nothing, which is the sweep-generated-zero-cases failure the epic rail names. Where the two providers legitimately DIFFER — the capability lists themselves, since the providers genuinely have different capabilities — assert the difference explicitly with a hand-written expected list rather than leaving it unasserted, so a capability silently vanishing from either side fails here.
implementationPlan.note: Added a 5-test parity suite comparing production Claude and Codex surfaces. It asserts both reconciled vocabularies non-empty before set equality; drives EXITED/SIGNALLED/UNOBSERVED through both production reconcilers; compares actual outcomes for the shared cancel/exit table; pins SUPPORTED|UNSUPPORTED and PROVEN|UNKNOWN set equality; compares frozen failure record keys/value types; and hand-pins both capability lists with the intentional Codex-only difference exactly [CWD_OBSERVATION]. Focused parity suite 1 file/5 tests and runner typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: Bridges, then verification and the mutation drill. Every non-test module under packages/runner/src/providers/codex/ needs its sibling .js bridge — the runner package now has 45+ of them and the claude modules all carry one, so the codex modules must too; a repo-wide runtime-loadability gate (task-535e773b) is landing that will enforce it. Content is EXACTLY one line, `export * from "./<name>.ts";`, LF, trailing newline — copy an existing claude bridge. The testkit corpus gets NO bridge, matching claude-golden-streams.ts. Verify bytes: final byte 0x0A, no 0x0D. Then run pnpm --filter @moe/runner test and pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test, stating before/after test AND suite counts as explicit numbers — count suites, because a file that fails to parse reports zero tests and reads as a pass. Mutation-verify one at a time, restoring between each: flip one nibble of the pinned corpus digest (both suites must fail at module load, before any assertion consumes the fixture — this is how Claude's was red-teamed); make an unproven capability default to SUPPORTED; remove the closure path sort; let a contradicting observation still report SUPPORTED; compute GAP over delivery order instead of the sequence set; drop the malformed-record-occupies-a-slot rule; add a command field to the render output. Every one must go red. Verify restores with git diff on the specific file, not git status (mem:mutation-drills-in-shared-worktree).
implementationPlan.note: TDD bridge gate first failed with exactly 8 missing Codex runtime modules, then passed 3/3 after adding the 8 exact LF one-line `.js` bridges. Binary audit: every bridge ends 0x0A, contains no 0x0D, and exactly equals `export * from "./<name>.ts";\n`; real Node 24 strip-types imports exposed non-empty exports for all 8, while `codex-probe.test.js` refused with literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. No testkit bridge was added. Baseline -> after counts are runner 30 files/980 tests -> 37 files/1040 tests, testkit 18 files/234 tests -> 19 files/239 tests. All 7 required production mutations went RED one at a time: a per-case pinned raw digest failed BOTH runner/testkit suites at module load (2 failed suites, 0 tests); unproven default SUPPORTED; closure sort removal; contradiction accepted; delivery-order GAP; malformed-slot removal; and render command field each failed its focused suite. Every mutation restored from an out-of-repo byte backup with before/after SHA-256 equality and path-specific git diff exit 0. Fresh post-restore runner 37/1040, testkit 19/239, and both typechecks exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial self-review, then commit. Read the diff as an attacker. Can any provider output reach a field that grants authority or satisfies verification — that is DoD 3, and the exact-sorted-key assertion on the render output is its proof, so re-check it covers every returned record and not just the top level. Can an unproven capability reach SUPPORTED by any path? Can a lying probe port crash the adapter instead of receiving a typed refusal? Is any returned record unfrozen or does any hold a Uint8Array? Grep the whole codex tree for the fence — child_process, spawn, .kill, Date.now, Math.random, new Date, performance.now — and expect ZERO code hits; the only permitted matches are doc comments stating the fence is not crossed. Confirm each production file is under 400 lines with wc -l, not PowerShell Measure-Object, which skips blank lines and only ever under-reports. Confirm no debug, probe or scratch file remains. Then commit by explicit pathspec only: `git status --porcelain` first, confirm every staged entry is under packages/runner/src/providers/codex or packages/testkit/src/providers/codex, unstage anything foreign with `git restore --staged --`, then `git commit -- packages/runner/src/providers/codex packages/testkit/src/providers/codex` and verify with `git show --stat`. BE AWARE: on the Claude adapter the harness auto-commit swept all 13 files into three FOREIGN tasks' commits before the worker's own commit ran (mem:gotcha-moe-wrapper-autocommit). If that happens again, verify content integrity with git show HEAD:<path> rather than rewriting history, and report it in the completion note — the epic rails forbid reset.
implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review read all 17 tracked Codex/testkit modules plus the 8 bridges from task-start base 82f4a354 and walked concurrency, hostile inputs, environmental assumptions, side effects, and output authority. The adapter is pure/no process control/shared mutation; final records are deeply frozen and byte fields are digest-bound base64, while exact render assertions cover all 9 top-level and all 7 layer keys with authority NONE/advisoryOnly true and no command/effect/lease/verification affordance. Unproven/contradictory probe paths remain typed UNSUPPORTED or stable refusals. Whole-tree fence grep has zero hits for child_process/spawn/.kill/time/random sources. wc -l reports every production file <400 (runner 97-216 lines; testkit corpus 262); no debug/scratch/TODO/only/skip artifacts. Review found a real bounded-input crash: Math.max(...262144 sequences) raised RangeError. TDD added a production-surface maximum-count case (RED RangeError, GREEN 13/13) and replaced spread with an O(n) min/max fold. Fresh post-review runner was 37 files/1091 tests, testkit 19/239, both typechecks exit 0 (runner total drift includes concurrent foreign tests). The harness had already swept the first 17 files into foreign commits 20c41a4 and 878538b; history was not rewritten. Explicit-path commit e21a3c1 contains the 8 bridges and overflow repair/test. HEAD byte audit matches all 25 scoped files and scoped diff is clean.

comments.content: Roadmap amendment 2026-08-07: the Codex adapter must consume the same provider-neutral validated skill snapshot and canonical AGENTS.md contract as Claude, record exact rendered bytes/digest, respect scoped instruction precedence, and never let skill or prompt text grant command/effect authority.

planSizeWarnings: Plan has 11 steps (target <=8); plans over 12 are rejected. Consider splitting the task before it grows.
Plan touches 9 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED — importing claudeFailure / ClaudeFailure into the codex adapter. It removes a duplicated ~10-line shape, but it couples two provider adapters that must be independently replaceable and puts a claude-named symbol on codex's rejection surface. Mirror structurally instead, and make step 9's parity test the thing that keeps them congruent — that converts an unenforced convention into a failing test.

REJECTED — extracting a shared providers/provider-contract.ts. Cleanest in the abstract, but it is not an owned path (owned paths are providers/codex/** and testkit providers/codex/** only), it would edit the proven Claude adapter, and task rail 1 says portability consumes frozen contracts. If a shared contract is genuinely wanted it is a separate task with both adapters in scope.

REJECTED — taking a @moe/skills dependency for the render input. It would touch packages/runner/package.json, outside owned paths, and make runner the first dependent of a package it needs only a shape from. Claude mirrors SkillRendererInput with the version literal pinned and catches drift by refusing on the literal; do the same.

REJECTED — SPIDR-splitting this into probe/stream/render tasks. It fits at 11 steps and 9 files with headroom under both hard thresholds, and a half-adapter cannot be parity-tested against Claude, which is the step that makes the mirroring trustworthy. Per epic rail 5 the projected diff size is explicitly NOT a reason to split.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MIRROR TARGET, verified on disk — packages/runner/src/providers/claude/ holds claude-observation.ts (300), claude-capabilities.ts (289), claude-probe.ts (120), claude-stream-anomalies.ts (265), claude-stream.ts (215), claude-render.ts (372), claude-cancel-reconcile.ts (131), each with a .js bridge already present. Both codex directories are greenfield, so there is no collision with anything in flight.

THE PRIOR HANDOFF IS THE MOST VALUABLE ARTEFACT HERE — mem:task-task-5ff2b39df70c4451ae07a44c92935b42-handoff records decisions that each fixed a real defect: closure sorted before hashing with duplicates refused; truthClass independent of pinningMethod; proof is observation not claim, and a self-contradicting record proves the opposite; GAP over the sequence SET with malformed records occupying a slot and COUNTER_REGRESSION suppressing analysis; bounded retention with unbounded digest coverage plus a separate event-count limit; renderedBase64 never Uint8Array; render output with no authority-bearing field, pinned by an exact sorted-key assertion. Read it before writing code, not after.

CROSS-PACKAGE CORPUS PROTOCOL — runner tests cannot import testkit TypeScript (rootDir "src" + composite). The corpus ships as one JSON document in a template literal between two exported marker constants; runner tests readFileSync, lastIndexOf both markers, slice, JSON.parse. Per-case sha256 is over RAW DECODED BYTES, not canonical JSON, specifically so the two packages' canonicalizers never have to agree.

BRIDGES — runner is fully bridged now (task-eb9ff081), so codex modules need theirs. Testkit is NOT fully bridged (15 .js against 41 non-test .ts) and claude-golden-streams.ts deliberately has none because it is not on the testkit entrypoint. Mirror that exactly; do not add one.

HUMAN AMENDMENT ON THIS TASK (2026-08-07) — the Codex adapter must consume the same provider-neutral validated skill snapshot and canonical AGENTS.md contract as Claude, record exact rendered bytes and digest, respect scoped instruction precedence, and never let skill or prompt text grant command or effect authority. It is a comment, not a DoD item, so it is easy to miss; step 7 carries it.
planningNotes.risks:
THE FENCE IS THE SECURITY PROPERTY — zero child_process, spawn, .kill, Date.now, Math.random in the whole adapter. Cancellation is an INPUT; process death is a caller-supplied observation with UNOBSERVED as a first-class arm that must never be collapsed into a guess. Launch locks, job-object death proof and relaunch belong to the supervisor, which this adapter feeds. Task rail 1 forbids an adapter forking lifecycle or authority semantics.

A PARITY TEST OVER EMPTY SETS PASSES — assert the compared vocabularies are non-empty BEFORE asserting set equality. This is precisely the 'a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes' defect the epic rail names, and a parity test is unusually prone to it.

WHERE THE PROVIDERS LEGITIMATELY DIFFER, ASSERT THE DIFFERENCE — the capability LISTS should not be equal, since the providers genuinely differ. Leaving that unasserted means a capability silently vanishing from either side is invisible. Pin both lists by hand.

UINT8ARRAY CRASHES AT CONSTRUCTION — Object.freeze throws on a non-empty typed array and runner's deepFreeze treats one as a plain record. Any bytes field must be base64. This is not a style preference; it is a runtime crash.

DIGEST-PINNED CORPUS FAILS AT MODULE LOAD — that is the desired behaviour and the red-team evidence: flipping one nibble must fail BOTH suites with 'no tests' before any assertion consumes the fixture. Count suites, not just tests, or that reads as a pass (mem:gotcha-mutation-drill-blind-to-broken-syntax).

HARNESS AUTO-COMMIT — on the Claude adapter the wrapper swept all 13 files into three FOREIGN tasks' commits before the worker's explicit-pathspec commit could run, leaving no commit of the worker's own (mem:gotcha-moe-wrapper-autocommit). Content was intact; only attribution was wrong. If it recurs, verify integrity with git show HEAD:<path>, report it, and do NOT rewrite history — the epic rails forbid reset.
